1.1. A. Wén Zhōngzǐ ***has written: 【0. 文中子 is the honorific posthumous name of WT. This text presents itself explicitly as a posthumous work. 1. This introduction 1.1.A is a written piece: this is not a report of what WT said in any context. It needs to be treated as concise learned composition rather than an oral discourse. 2. In fact, this reads very much like a very personal author's introduction to a 《續論語》envisaged by WT himself. But it may evidently be a later composition by enthusiastic family members and admirers of WT. 3.The frame of this is emphatic/emotional in both the initial and the final lines. 4. The question arises, to what extent the rest of the entries in this book are written compositions as opposed to reported dialogues. This question needs to be faced case by case with regard to each entry.]

“The rot of the Six States,28 the cruelty of fallen Qin —

I cannot bear even to hear of them; how should I take from them the bond of kingly rule?29 When the Han unified the realm, did it not sweep away the remnants of savagery and filth, make a fresh start with the people, and rouse their eyes and ears?” Xue Shou said: “And may I ask why the Continued Odes spans all the Six Dynasties?” The Master said: “You ask because Confucius’s Three Hundred30 begin and end with Zhou?” Shou said: “Yes.” The Master said: “How should I dare aspire to Confucius! Master Wenzhong said: “For three hundred years32 the realm has had no reward and punishment.33 Could the Classic of the Prime then not be made?” Xue Shou said: “Why does it begin with Emperor Hui of Jin?”34 The Master said: “In antiquity, with enlightened kings above, could reward and punishment have gone astray? The praise and blame of the Classic of the Prime stand in the place of reward and punishment — is it not because the realm has no master, and reward and punishment have lost their light?” Xue Shou said: “Then the Spring and Autumn, beginning with King Ping of Zhou and Duke Yin of Lu35 — was its purpose also such as this?” The Master said: “It was! — and no one knows it.”36 Xue Shou said: “Now at last I understand: when the realm is ordered, the sage stands above; when the realm is in chaos, the sage stands below. The sage in power carries out reward and punishment; the sage in obscurity composes praise and blame. Thus is the August Ultimate raised anew, and this culture37 not lost. Is it not profound?” He bowed twice and went out, and told Master Dong. Dong said: “Confucius is gone — does this culture now reside here?”

“Now at last I understand: when the realm is ordered, the sage stands above; when the realm is in chaos, the sage stands below. The sage in power carries out reward and punishment; the sage in obscurity composes praise and blame. Thus is the August Ultimate raised anew, and this culture37 not lost. Is it not profound?” He bowed twice and went out, and told Master Dong. Dong said: “Confucius is gone — does this culture now reside here?”
